parsedVerdict.reasoning: BorrowBookUseCase passes: everything in it is application-layer orchestration. `execute` loads aggregates through repository ports, throws DomainError when a book or member doesn't exist, and gets the time and new IDs from the Clock and IdGenerator ports. It leaves the borrowing rule to the domain service (`LoanPolicy.assertCanBorrow`) and the state changes to the domain (`book.checkOut()`, `Loan.open`). It then saves through the ports and maps the result to a DTO. The file has no persistence code, no HTTP or framework handling, and no hand-written business rules. One borderline item: the constant `STANDARD_PERIOD = LoanPeriod.ofDays(21)` is a business setting that could arguably live in LoanPolicy. However, it is only passed into a domain factory as a use-case setting and is not evaluated here, so it doesn't amount to a misplaced business rule. `ExecuteContextDto` carries an optional requestId that is never used. It is generic call metadata with no tie to any framework, so it isn't transport logic.
